instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the night before: cut a quarter of the cucumber into small dice and put it in a small covered container in the fridge. Peel the rest of the cucumber and cut it into chunks.
Core the 2.5 lb tomatoes and cut them into chunks. Seed the red pepper. Cut half of it into chunks, dice the other half small and add it to the container with the diced cucumber.
Peel a quarter of the red onion and rinse it under cold water. Peel the 2 garlic cloves. Pick 1/4 cup of cilantro leaves and keep the rest of the bunch in the fridge.

Put the tomatoes in the blender first, then the cucumber chunks, pepper chunks, onion, garlic and cilantro leaves. Add 3 tbsp sherry vinegar, the 1 1/4 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. If it doesn't all fit, blend it in two batches.
Blend on high and pour in 1/2 cup of the olive oil while it runs. Keep going for about a minute, until it's completely smooth and turns a pale orange red.
Pour it into a jug or a bowl, cover it and chill it for at least 2 hours, until it's properly cold.
When you're ready to eat, stir it and taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt or a few more drops of vinegar.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and chop a small handful of the cilantro.
Ladle it into bowls, or into jars for packed lunches. Top with the diced cucumber and pepper, the cherry tomatoes and the chopped cilantro, and drizzle over the last 2 tbsp of olive oil.
advance_prep_notes: Blend and chill it at least 2 hours ahead, or the night before.
method_notes: Both versions blend raw ripe tomato, cucumber, red pepper, a little red onion, garlic, sherry vinegar and olive oil with no bread, and serve it cold with diced cucumber and a drizzle of oil on top. Love and Lemons blends everything straight away with half a cup of oil and some cilantro, then chills it for 2 hours. RecipeTin Eats leaves the chopped vegetables to marinate for 3 to 24 hours before blending, uses less oil and offers straining for a smoother, thinner soup. This one follows Love and Lemons, using its red bell pepper option in place of fresno chiles so the base stays mild.
